references_experience.text: ncil can continue to fulfil its statutory function of distributing public funding to the arts sector securely, reliably, and efficiently. The objective of this procurement is to secure a modern, cloud-hosted, configurable off-the-shelf Grant Management System capable of supporting the full grant lifecycle for applicants, assessors, panellists, and Arts Council staff. The solution will provide a secure and accessible digital platform for application management, assessment workflows, award administration, post-award monitoring, reporting, and integration with the Arts Council’s existing Finance Management System. The organisation's strategic preference is for a solution that requires minimal custom development and can be configured using standard platform functionality. The replacement programme will be delivered through a phased implementation approach centred on the successful completion of a Proof of Concept (PoC) using a live Arts Council funding programme. This approach is intended to validate vendor capability, system performance, user experience, and organisational readiness before progressing to full production deployment. The Arts Council is seeking a long-term technology partner capable of delivering a proven solution while supporting a structured, low-risk transition from the e

Background and Objective The Arts Council is undertaking the replacement of its existing Grant Management System (GMS), a critical business application that underpins the administration, assessment, award, and ongoing management of public funding programmes. The current platform has been in operation beyond its supported lifecycle for over a decade and now presents significant operational, cybersecurity, governance, and business continuity risks. The replacement programme has therefore been established primarily as a risk mitigation and service continuity initiative to ensure the Arts Council can continue to fulfil its statutory function of distributing public funding to the arts sector securely, reliably, and efficiently. The objective of this procurement is to secure a modern, cloud-hosted, configurable off-the-shelf Grant Management System capable of supporting the full grant lifecycle for applicants, assessors, panellists, and Arts Council staff. The solution will provide a secure and accessible digital platform for application

e, user experience, and organisational readiness before progressing to full production deployment. The Arts Council is seeking a long-term technology partner capable of delivering a proven solution while supporting a structured, low-risk transition from the existing environment. The new system must support bilingual service delivery (Irish and English), modern digital user experiences, robust security controls, workflow automation, management reporting, and interoperability with current and future finance platforms. The solution should also align with public sector best practice, including cloud-first principles, accessibility requirements, data protection obligations, cybersecurity standards, and emerging NIS2 requirements. 1. Introduction

The African Union Development Agency – New Partnership for Africa Development (AUDA-NEPAD) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the “Resilient Irrigation for a Sustainable Economy Project”, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. “Consultancy Services to Develop and Deploy the Africa RISE Gateway”

 

  1. Description of Services

The consulting services (“the Services”) include: Task 1: Africa RISE User Requirements Assessment: Map and profile all user groups and partners including relevant African Union agencies and departments (AUDANEPAD, AU-SAFGRAD, SEBE), government ministries, transboundary water management agencies, regulators, MPA focal points, implementing partners, research institutes and universities and technical experts, farmers, aggregators, private sector, equipment suppliers and financial institutions and farmer unions and cooperative societies etc; Task 2: Design, Develop and Commission the Africa RISE Gateway: Define system architecture, data structures, modules, dashboard requirements and proc

ISE User Requirements Assessment: Map and profile all user groups and partners including relevant African Union agencies and departments (AUDANEPAD, AU-SAFGRAD, SEBE), government ministries, transboundary water management agencies, regulators, MPA focal points, implementing partners, research institutes and universities and technical experts, farmers, aggregators, private sector, equipment suppliers and financial institutions and farmer unions and cooperative societies etc; Task 2: Design, Develop and Commission the Africa RISE Gateway: Define system architecture, data structures, modules, dashboard requirements and process workflows, including a unified data interoperability Layer that meets vPIC standards and aligns with the Africa RISE Regional Geospatial Analytics Platform and national irrigation monitoring systems.  The architecture shall specify: (a) the endpoints and payload schemas through which national data collection tools, the Regional Geospatial Platform,  and other authorized external data sources submit and validate benchmarking data; (b) the data lineage and version control mechanisms ensuring that published benchmarks are traceable to their submission source; and (c) the traffic-light alert logic that translates performanc

sociated training materials for all user groups, comprising: (i) a Technical Track for AUDA-NEPAD IT personnel, national technical focal points and system administrators, covering system administration, data management, integration and cybersecurity; (ii) an Operational Track for programme managers, extension officers and policy stakeholders, focusing on effective use of the platform and its functional modules; and (iii) an End-User Track providing simplified guidance and orientation materials. Task 4: Sustainable Operation and Maintenance (O&M) Model for the Gateway: Assess the technical and operational requirements for sustained operation of the Gateway, including hosting, security, data management, updates, user support and maintenance schedules and prepare indicative annual cost projections for the post-project period. Task 5: Envisaged functionality of the Africa RISE Gateway: The Africa RISE Gateway, as a go-to information and knowledge solution, is envisaged to serve.

ip_data_security.text: the cost of services needed to operate and maintain NLS’s My Talking Books (an Amazon Alexa skill) in production. My Talking Books is an Amazon Alexa skill that enables NLS patrons to search the NLS collection, browse the NLS collection, retrieve/manage the patron’s Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) Wishlist, stream NLS talking books, and manage the patron’s Bookshelf using a voice-only interface available on Alexa-enabled commercial smart-speaker platforms. The contractor shall be responsible for providing RealSAM Dialog licenses and services required to operate the system in production, while meeting all IT information-system security requirements as required by the Library of Congress. C.2 BACKGROUND NLS administers a free program that loans audio and braille books and magazines, music scores in braille and large print, and specially designed audio-playback and refreshable-braille-display equipment to residents of the United States who are unable to read or use standard print materials due to visual or physical impairment. NLS administers the program nationally, while direct service to eligible individuals and institutions is the responsibility of cooperating network libraries in the various states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, Guam, and the U. S. Virgin Islands. Thi

hall provide the Library with license and technical support. This support shall be provided on an annual basis at a firm-fixed price. This support shall be provided in blocks of 500. This support service must ensure that users with legacy RealSAM Dialog licenses can use the My Talking Books skill in production. The contractor shall provide the Library with a price schedule (Attachment J3 - Pricing Chart.xlsx) for the following scenarios: A. RealSAM Dialog License Support – An annual fee for blocks of 500 perpetual user licenses for the RealSAM dialog engine. This scenario reflects the current state of affairs where the contractor is hosting all required non-GFE services (Auth Proxy, Streaming Servers, Dialog Engine, etc.). B. RealSAM Dialog License Support with Auth Proxy hosted by the Library – same as scenario A, but the Library would host the Auth Proxy service instead of the contractor. C. RealSAM Legacy Dialog License Support with Auth Proxy and Streaming Servers hosted by the Library – same as scenario A, but the Library would host both the Auth Proxy service and Streaming Servers instead of the contractor. Τσερκέζη 20, 68200 Ορεστιάδα  25520 27900  25520 27757  info@eeabe.gr / director@eeabe.gr URL https://eeabe.gr/online/ Πληροφορίες: Πετρέσης Γεώργιος ΠΡΟΣΚΛΗΣΗ ΥΠΟΒΟΛΗΣ ΠΡΟΣΦΟΡΑΣ ΜΕ ΤΗ ΔΙΑΔΙΚΑΣΙΑ ΤΗΣ ΑΠΕΥΘΕΙΑΣ ΑΝΑΘΕΣΗΣ ΘΕΜΑ: Πρόσκληση υποβολής προσφοράς για την παροχή υπηρεσιών «Provision of Information, Publicity, and Communication Services for the CHANGE4PLANET Project» , στο πλαίσιο της Πράξης «Second Chance for Product and Planet – CHANGE4PLANET», MIS 6010809.. CPV: 79413000-2 – Υπηρεσίες παροχής συμβουλών σε θέματα μάρκετινγκ Η Εταιρεία Έρευνας και Ανάπτυξης Βορείου Έβρου Α.Ε. – Αναπτυξιακή Ανώνυμη Εταιρεία Ο.Τ.Α. (ΕΕΑΒΕ Α.Ε.), ως Επικεφαλής Δικαιούχος (Lead Beneficiary) της Πράξης

δικαιολογητικό που προβλέπεται από την ισχύουσα νομοθεσία για την ολοκλήρωση της διαδικασίας ανάθεσης. ΙΣΧΥΣ ΠΡΟΣΦΟΡΑΣ Η προσφορά θα ισχύει και θα δεσμεύει τον προσφέροντα για [30] ημέρες από την επομένη της καταληκτικής ημερομηνίας υποβολής της. ΤΡΟΠΟΣ ΚΑΙ ΠΡΟΘΕΣΜΙΑ ΥΠΟΒΟΛΗΣ Η προσφορά θα πρέπει να υποβληθεί μέχρι και την Πέμπτη 10 Σεπτεμβρίου 2026 και ώρα 14:00, στην έδρα της ΕΕΑΒΕ Α.Ε., Σωτηρίου Τσερκέζη 20, Ορεστιάδα, Τ.Κ. 68200. . Η προσφορά μπορεί να κατατεθεί: • αυτοπροσώπως, • μέσω εξουσιοδοτημένου εκπροσώπου, • ταχυδρομικά με συστημένη επιστολή ή • μέσω ιδιωτικού ταχυδρομείου (courier) ή • μέσω email στο invitationseeabe@gmail.com , δηλώνοντας τον αριθμό Πρωτοκόλλου της Πρόσκλησης στο θεμα. BACKGROUND The Department of the Air Force Art Collection is comprised of over 9,000 paintings, works on paper, mixed media, textiles, and sculptures spanning from World War I to the present day. To ensure the long-term preservation and security of a specific portion of this historic collection, the NMUSAF requires temporary, climate- controlled on-site storage for 992 designated artworks at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB). Due to inadequate historical storage conditions at their previous location, all 992 of these specific artworks have experienced prior mold damage. To mitigate risk and contain the issue, all assets will be securely wrapped and packaged in protective materials prior to being placed into the storage containers, preventing any further spread of mold.
